Estimated marginal means, contrasts, and slopes tables

Source: R/modelbased.R
apa_means.Rd

Makes APA-style tables of estimated marginal means, contrasts between them (e.g., pairwise comparisons after an ANOVA), and simple slopes (e.g., to probe a moderation effect), computed with the modelbased package.

Usage

apa_means(
  fit,
  by = NULL,
  ...,
  starred = NA,
  bolded = NA,
  column_formats = NULL,
  format_variable_names = TRUE
)

apa_contrasts(
  fit,
  contrast = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  ...,
  effect_size = NULL,
  sd = NULL,
  starred = NA,
  bolded = NA,
  column_formats = NULL,
  format_variable_names = TRUE
)

apa_slopes(
  fit,
  trend = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  ...,
  johnson_neyman = NULL,
  starred = NA,
  bolded = NA,
  column_formats = NULL,
  format_variable_names = TRUE
)

Arguments

fit

a model, or output of modelbased::estimate_means() (for apa_means()), modelbased::estimate_contrasts() (for apa_contrasts()), or modelbased::estimate_slopes() (for apa_slopes())

by

variables whose levels (or values) the estimates are computed at (e.g., by = Species, by = c(am, cyl), by = "hp=[sd]", or by = list(hp = "[sd]")). Variable names can be quoted or unquoted, but values (e.g., "hp=[fivenum]") must be quoted. In apa_means() and apa_slopes(), the last variable labels the rows and the others get heading rows; in apa_contrasts(), all of them get heading rows. Passed to the modelbased function.

...

other arguments passed to the modelbased function when fit is a model (e.g., p_adjust = "holm", predict = "link", or estimate = "average")

starred

columns to which significance stars are added (e.g., "p" or "Estimate")

bolded

columns that are bolded when p \(\le\) .05

column_formats

column_formats() object. If NULL (default), the defaults are used. The estimate column is named "Estimate".

format_variable_names

if TRUE (default), variable names are formatted (e.g., "Sepal.Length" becomes "Sepal Length"). Factor levels are shown as they are.

contrast

variable whose levels (or values) are compared (e.g., contrast = cyl), quoted or unquoted. Passed to modelbased::estimate_contrasts().

effect_size

in apa_contrasts(), whether to add Cohen's d and its confidence interval. If NULL (default), d is added when it can be computed (models of continuous outcomes with an identity link, such as lm(), or any model when sd is given). If TRUE, an error is given when it cannot be computed.

sd

in apa_contrasts(), the standard deviation that differences are divided by to compute Cohen's d. If NULL (default), the model's residual standard deviation is used (not for mixed models).

trend

predictor whose slopes are estimated (e.g., trend = wt), quoted or unquoted. Passed to modelbased::estimate_slopes().

johnson_neyman

in apa_slopes(), whether the note gives the Johnson-Neyman intervals. If NULL (default), they are given when they can be computed (see Details). If TRUE, an error is given when they cannot be computed.

Value

apa7_tbl (tibble)

Details

fit is either a model or the output of modelbased::estimate_means(), modelbased::estimate_contrasts(), or modelbased::estimate_slopes(). With a model, by, contrast, trend, and the arguments in ... (e.g., p_adjust) are passed to the modelbased function, so apa_contrasts(fit, contrast = "group", p_adjust = "holm") is the same as apa_contrasts(modelbased::estimate_contrasts(fit, contrast = "group", p_adjust = "holm")).

Rows are labeled by the levels of the last focal variable (in apa_means()), by the levels compared (in apa_contrasts(), e.g., "6 \(-\) 4"), or by the levels of the moderator (in apa_slopes()). Any other variables in by get heading rows, with the rows below them indented. Numeric levels (e.g., values of a continuous moderator) are rounded to 2 decimals.

Values set with a modelbased shortcut are named, with the value in parentheses: "x=[sd]" (or "x=[meansd]") gives "\(-\)1SD", "M", and "+1SD"; "x=[mad]" gives "\(-\)1MAD", "Mdn", and "+1MAD"; "x=[fivenum]" gives "Min", "Q~1~", "Mdn", "Q~3~", and "Max"; "x=[quartiles]" gives "Q~1~", "Mdn", and "Q~3~"; and "x=[minmax]" gives "Min" and "Max". Contrasts between such values (e.g., contrast = "x=[sd]") are labeled by name (e.g., "+1SD \(-\) M"), and the note gives the values. With a model, a numeric variable named in by without values (e.g., by = "x") is set to its mean and 1 SD above and below it, as with by = "x=[sd]" (rather than the modelbased default of 10 values, which suits plots better than tables).

apa_note() says what the values are, how the other predictors were held constant, on which scale the estimates are (for models with a link function, such as logistic regression), which level was subtracted from which, and how p-values were adjusted for multiple comparisons.

In apa_contrasts(), contrasts from models of continuous outcomes with an identity link (e.g., lm() and aov()) get Cohen's d with its confidence interval: each difference divided by the model's residual standard deviation (\(\hat{\sigma}\)), as in emmeans::eff_size(). The interval accounts for the uncertainty in \(\hat{\sigma}\). For mixed models, there is no single right standard deviation to divide by, so d is shown only when it is given with sd (e.g., the square root of the sum of the variance components and the residual variance). d is not computed for logistic and other generalized linear models.

In apa_slopes(), when the slope of trend depends on a single continuous moderator in by through a two-way interaction (e.g., lm(y ~ x * m)), the note gives the Johnson-Neyman intervals (Johnson & Neyman, 1936): the values of the moderator, within its observed range, at which the slope is significant. The boundaries are computed exactly from the coefficients and their covariance matrix (the values of the moderator at which the slope's test statistic equals its critical value), with t and the residual degrees of freedom for lm() models and the normal distribution for other models (e.g., mixed models). They are not computed for models with a link function (e.g., logistic regression), or when the slope also depends on other variables (e.g., a three-way interaction).

Bayesian models are not yet supported.

References

Benjamini, Y., & Hochberg, Y. (1995). Controlling the false discovery rate: A practical and powerful approach to multiple testing. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Methodological), 57(1), 289–300. doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x

Holm, S. (1979). A simple sequentially rejective multiple test procedure. Scandinavian Journal of Statistics, 6(2), 65–70.

Johnson, P. O., & Neyman, J. (1936). Tests of certain linear hypotheses and their application to some educational problems. Statistical Research Memoirs, 1, 57–93.

Kramer, C. Y. (1956). Extension of multiple range tests to group means with unequal numbers of replications. Biometrics, 12(3), 307–310. doi:10.2307/3001469

Tukey, J. W. (1994). The problem of multiple comparisons. In H. I. Braun (Ed.), The collected works of John W. Tukey: Vol. VIII. Multiple comparisons, 1948–1983 (pp. 1–300). Chapman & Hall.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("modelbased", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("marginaleffects", quietly = TRUE)) {
  fit <- lm(Sepal.Width ~ Species * Sepal.Length, data = iris)

  # Means of each species, with sepal length held at its mean
  apa_means(fit, by = "Species")

  # Pairwise comparisons, with Holm-adjusted p-values
  apa_contrasts(fit, contrast = "Species", p_adjust = "holm")

  # Simple slopes of sepal length in each species
  apa_slopes(fit, trend = "Sepal.Length", by = "Species")

  # The output of modelbased works, too
  modelbased::estimate_contrasts(fit, contrast = "Species") |>
    apa_contrasts() |>
    apa_note()
}
#> [1] "Values are differences between estimated marginal means of Sepal Width (the first level minus the second). Sepal Length is held at its mean (5.84). *d* = difference divided by the residual standard deviation of the model (0.27); its confidence interval accounts for the uncertainty in the residual standard deviation. *p*-values are not adjusted for multiple comparisons. CI = confidence interval."
